chunks: My father, my brother, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on them all, narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

I and 'Amir ibn 'Abdillah ibn Judh'ah al-Azdi were with Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him). 'Amir said to him, 'People claim that the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) was buried in al-Rahbah.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No.' 'Amir asked, 'So where was he buried?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'When he died, al-Hasan (peace be upon him) carried him and brought him to the rear of Kufah, close to al-Najaf, to the left of al-Ghari and to the right of al-Hirah. He was buried among white gravel. I said, 'Afterwards, I went to the location and presumed I had found a place from it, then I came to him and informed him.' He said, 'You were right, you were right, three times. May Allah have mercy on you.' [You were right, may Allah have mercy on you, three times.]
ai.seo_question: Where is the grave of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) located according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Kamil al-Ziyarat establishes the authenticity of Imam Ali’s (a.s.) burial in Najaf, correcting the prevalent view of al-Rahbah by detailing the specific topographical markers—white gravel—used for identification. The confirmation by Safwan al-Jammal underscores the reliability of the Ahl al-Bayt’s direct knowledge of the site, which later became a central shrine for Shia pilgrimage and spiritual reflection.
